title: Adaptive dequantization throttle and cross-lane kernel probe for mixed-precision paths
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Dequantization overhead at the boundary between INT8/FP8 kernels and mixed-precision decode contributes a variable but significant fraction of end-to-end decode latency for interactive workloads. For short-to-medium sequences (16-128 tokens) we observe up to 20-35% of per-request CPU/GPU time spent in dequant/requant work and memory copies when the runtime switches kernel lanes or when KV cache layouts force copy-on-write during prefill. This is especially visible under bursty, low-concurrency traffic where batching knobs are limited.

Goal: Reduce dequant/requant wall-time and memory churn while preserving numerical fidelity for a set of verified models. Target improvements: reduce decode-path dequant overhead by at least 30% (absolute), bring p50 decode latency for seq=64 down by ~20% on A100 targets in our canary workload, and avoid increasing memory footprint by more than 5%.

Proposal: Implement an "adaptive dequantization throttle" plus a lightweight "cross-lane kernel probe" step in the runtime kernel selection pipeline. Key ideas: (1) Lazy and windowed dequantization — delay full dequant of layer activations until decode reaches steady-state for a request (avoid dequant during short prefill bursts); (2) Throttle concurrent dequant operations across worker threads to avoid memory spike and PCIe saturation; (3) Cross-lane probe — at model load / first-prefill, run microbench probes for a small set of representative sequence-lengths (8, 32, 64) and batch sizes to determine whether the INT8/FP8 fused kernels or the mixed-precision FP16 path yields lower end-to-end latency given the observed KV cache layout; (4) Mixed-precision handoff hints — expose a short-lived hint in the request context when the probe indicates a lane flip is beneficial so that subsequent requests in the same session can avoid repeated probes; (5) Requant fusion improvements — combine small per-layer requant/scale ops into single epilogue kernels for contiguous layers to reduce kernel launch overhead.

Design details:
- Runtime hook: extend kernel_selector to include a probe phase run once per model process (configurable TTL). Probe results cached in memory and in on-disk model-profile metadata.
- Throttling: global token-based semaphore controlling concurrent dequant tasks. Semaphore size chosen from probe throughput metrics and auto-tuned at startup based on GPU memory headroom.
- Lazy dequant: for attention prefill we keep activations in packed int8 buffer and only dequant a rolling window of last N layers (N adaptive: smaller during warmup). This reduces immediate memory copies during prefill-heavy workloads at the cost of slightly more complex KV indexing.
- Handoff: when probe shows mixed-precision provides clear latency win, annotate subsequent decode requests with a HINT_USE_FP16 flag for up to M requests or T seconds.

Trade-offs and risk:
- Risk: delayed dequant increases complexity in KV indexing and could increase tail latency if heuristics misfire. Mitigation: conservative defaults, metrics to detect misfires, and automatic fallback to safe path.
- Correctness: FP8/INT8 scaling edge cases — we will run targeted numeric regression suites (existing eval prompts + adversarial tokenization cases) before enabling default canary.
- ABI: changes to fused epilogue kernels may affect model binaries; we will keep an ABI compatibility shim and require release gating.

Testing and rollout plan:
1) Microbench kernels (unit tests + perf harness) - PR to runtime repo for fused requant epilogue (internal PR #6421).
2) Integrate probe + throttle in a feature branch, enable behind runtime flag.
3) Canary: enable on a 5% traffic slice for dedicated and hosted canaries, monitor latency p50/p95, memory ops, and CPU/GPU utilization.
4) Evaluate with eval-suite: numeric regressions, hallucination rate checks on known prompts.
5) Gradual rollout with A/B telemetry and automatic rollback on perf regressions.

Telemetry and signals:
- New metrics: dequant_time_ms (per-request), dequant_memcpy_bytes, probe_decision (INT8|FP8|FP16), dequant_throttle_wait_ms.
- Dashboards: canary vs baseline comparison for p50/p95 decode latencies, memory footprint delta, and token throughput.

Acceptance criteria:
- p50 decode latency for seq=64 reduced by >=15% in canary at same concurrency and batch settings.
- dequant_time_ms reduced by >=30% on average across sampled traffic.
- No numeric regression >0.5% on targeted eval prompts.

Links to artifacts and context: see attachments for design doc and perf traces.
comments: 2026-02-12 Sofia Alvarez: Initial triage — measurement confirmed. Attached microbench results for A100 and RTX8000. Noted that prefill-heavy traces show highest dequant costs.

2026-02-20 Jamal Reed: Prototype of semaphore-based throttling submitted. Early microbench shows 18% p50 latency reduction for seq=64 when throttling concurrent dequant to 4. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421
2026-02-28 Design review (Priya): Concern about KV indexing complexity. Action: add index mapping tests and a fallback hot path. Priya approved the canary plan after seeing profiling data.

2026-03-05 QA (Miguel): Numeric regression suite run against the FP8 path; observed a 0.3% drift in one adversarial prompt. Marked as acceptable by SRE after double-checking seed handling. Added a test to catch it in CI.

2026-03-11 Performance review: Integrated the cross-lane probe, auto-tune settles semaphore=6 on A100-40GB for default canary workload. Measured dequant_time_ms drop from 14.2ms -> 9.1ms (36% improvement) on sampled requests.
2026-03-14 Jamal Reed: Merging feature branch into staging for canary rollout. Next steps: enable flags on canary pool and monitor dashboards (owner: Jamal).
notes: Bench targets: decode p50 <= 42ms for seq=64 on A100-40GB with dynamic batching; dequant CPU/GPU overhead <= 12% of decode path
Canary gating: rollback if p95 increases by >10% or numeric regressions >0.5% on eval-suite
